items.item: work_mem budgets both sorts and hash tables; sort operations are used for ORDER BY, DISTINCT, and merge joins
Parallel aggregation's two-stage design: a Partial Aggregate node per worker, a Finalize Aggregate node on the leader
Parallel aggregation is unfavorable when groups are many relative to input rows
Parallel aggregation is not supported when an aggregate contains DISTINCT or ORDER BY, or for GROUPING SETS
Plans add nodes above scans for aggregation, joining, sorting and other operations

items.item: Why hash aggregation wins decisively at low group cardinality, measured directly rather than asserted
That the hash-vs-sort crossover is a real, measured result on this topic's own schema — the planner's own default choice (HashAggregate) was not the faster plan at high cardinality
Why sort cost tracks rows while hash cost (once spilling) tracks groups relative to available memory, as the structural explanation for the crossover
Reading a HashAggregate's batch/partition count off EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) as the signal that it spilled, the same signal topic 21 used for a spilling hash join

That the finalize step of a parallel aggregate plan is a GroupAggregate (streaming aggregation over sorted partial results), not a second HashAggregate — read directly from this topic's own measured plan
Why a DISTINCT aggregate takes a sort-based path rather than a hash-based one, confirmed by this topic's own measured plan rather than inferred from the docs alone

items.item: GROUPING SETS as a case parallel aggregation excludes entirely, named from the documented exclusion rather than measured directly in this session
Eager aggregation pushed below joins as a named PostgreSQL 19 beta feature this topic could not measure on its PostgreSQL 16 instance, left as a pointer rather than an unverified claim
Why adding parallel workers isn't a universal fix for a slow aggregate, specifically when groups are a large fraction of rows
When to reach for enable_hashagg=off on a specific query rather than trusting the planner's own default choice, given this topic's own measured counter-example
